title: How basketball (1891) and volleyball (1895) were invented at YMCA schools in Massachusetts

sources.title: Where Basketball was Invented: The History of Basketball

sources.publisher: National YMCA Hall of Fame at Springfield College
sources.title: History (YMCA timeline)
Professor discovers only known audio recording of James Naismith

facts.text: James Naismith was a young instructor at the International YMCA Training School (now Springfield College) in Springfield, Massachusetts.
Naismith set up the first basketball game in December 1891.
His supervisor Luther Gulick asked him to invent a new indoor game that could be played in winter.
Students had to stay indoors during the long New England winter, and the required gym work was dull.
Naismith mixed in elements of rugby, soccer, lacrosse and a children's game called duck on a rock.
He asked the janitor for two boxes to use as goals, but the janitor brought two peach baskets.
The baskets were nailed to the lower balcony rail of the gym, which was ten feet high.
The bottoms of the baskets were not cut out until a few years later.
The first games were played with an old soccer ball.
Naismith later recalled that the first game turned violent because he had not made enough rules.
William Morgan, a Springfield College graduate (class of 1894), invented volleyball at the YMCA in Holyoke, Massachusetts, in 1895.
Morgan was a YMCA physical education instructor who thought basketball was too strenuous for businessmen.
Morgan combined elements of basketball with tennis and handball.
Morgan first called the game mintonette.
In 1896, at an exhibition at the Springfield school, the game was renamed volley ball because the ball goes back and forth over the net.
